rules.rationale: Strongest source refractive-index driver; Moss relation links its high polarizability to narrow experimental gaps.
Heavy polarizable ions lower conduction-band edges, shrinking gaps despite their source refractive-index gain.
Chalcogen p states raise the valence-band maximum, yielding smaller measured gaps than oxides.
Halogen dominance depressed source refractive index, but its ionicity and deep anion states widen gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Sign-reversed transfer of the source refractive-index effects via the Moss relation: polarizable, heavy, metalloid or chalcogen chemistries raise n yet narrow gaps. Weakens if experimental gaps here are set by structure or measurement rather than composition.

rules.rationale: Balanced heavy compositions favor wide-gap insulating ordered phases rather than narrow-gap intermetallics.
Fluoride and chloride anions are highly electronegative, deepening valence bands and enlarging ionic gaps.
Closed-shell s-block cations donate weakly and form ionic insulators with wide experimental gaps.
Localized f manifolds add mid-gap transitions and narrow measured optical gaps in lanthanide compounds.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis to the inverted-Moss skill: among the high mean-Z population, balanced and s-block ionic chemistries still yield wide gaps rather than narrow ones. Fails if heavy narrow-gap intermetallics dominate the top of the target distribution.

lesson: The same-sign domain skill underperformed badly (mean AUC 58.0 versus 82.5), losing on five of eight seeds, so the sign-reversed Moss transfer from the source refractive-index evidence is the better bet. Its scale-free rules survived the halide-dominant pool here, though its components remain uncertain because the source confidences are low.
revision_summary: Retained and sharpened the source-grounded inverted-transfer skill and made it the deployment choice based on the development-seed feedback; downgraded the previous same-sign wide-gap skill into a counter-hypothesis with weakened weights. Each skill uses four rules over exact catalog field/value pairs, with one mechanistically justified two-condition interaction. Two-condition rules were limited to one per skill. All parameters stay inside the allowed ranges, rationales under 25 words and hypotheses under 45 words. No target outcomes were accessed.
